From the moment you step in, you’re welcomed by an impeccable ambience — a perfect blend of elegance, comfort, and sophistication. The floor-to-ceiling windows and serene sea views add a refreshing openness to the space, making it an ideal spot for both casual evenings and special occasions.

The food is equally impressive — beautifully presented and full of flavor. Whether you’re indulging in light bites or a full meal, the quality and attention to detail are consistent throughout. The drinks menu is well-curated, offering a range of classic cocktails, premium spirits, and innovative concoctions that are crafted to perfection by the skilled bartenders.

The service is exactly what you’d expect from the Taj — warm, attentive, and unobtrusive. Whether you’re meeting friends or winding down after a long day, the Atrium offers a luxurious yet relaxed experience that’s hard to match in the city.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy great food and drinks in a stunning, tranquil setting., name_person=Dr. Minal Kabra}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a week ago, review=The hospitality given by Ashwini was amazing she was a good host and a very kind soul enjoyed my high tea a lot  helped me taking pictures of the high tea experience .Thanks for the most welcoming and warm hospitality experience., name_person=Zoya Lakdawala}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Omg
So today I visited Taj Lands End,Bandra.
The much awaited visit.
I was super excited, for the visit.
First we went to Vista,  no one even bothered to ask about the order, forget a glass of water.
Families who were done with their lunch, were still sitting there and screaming on top of their voice as if some wedding reception.
We left the place, went to  Atrium,again ,guests who were lounging there were so loud.
The music was so loud.
The AC was not working.
No one bothered to offer a glass of water,  finally we gave our order for tea and fish fingers.
Water still didn't arrive.
Tea came without milk and sugar.
After askin three times for sugar, finally it came, but milk didn't arrive.
I had the tea without milk and just came out.
Didn't expect this from Taj.
I'm a Taj loyalist.
God if you have patience, visit, otherwise don't.

Never came across such indecent behaviour by  female staff in TAJ ever anywhere in the world  ! This cafe really needs to be shut down!, name_person=Kanak Misra}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Other, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=We stayed at the hotel and decided to use the Atrium lounge on a few nights as it was quiet and served drinks until 1am. The atmosphere was good; however, the service and entertainment need significant improvement. The singers were not very good, which sounds harsh, but it's the truth.

The service was the main letdown. Even on quiet nights, when we were literally the only table, the service was extremely slow. One night, it took over 20 minutes to get one whiskey, and a further 35 minutes to get a refill. On the next night, it took over 30 minutes to get two English breakfast teas. However, the bill was produced with record speed—68 seconds when requested one night. On some nights, we didn't even have to request the bill; it was eagerly presented to us with the card machine 20 minutes before closing time. Even though we waited patiently for our drinks, they couldn't extend the same courtesy and let us finish those drinks before requesting payment.

I didn't try the food at the Atrium lounge, so I cannot comment on that. I'd advise going to the pool bar on floor L2, where the service is much better, even though they have far fewer staff., name_person=Tj}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Other, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Grilled_Vegetables], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=10 months ago, review=I visited Taj on February 14th and booked a sea-facing suite room for one day. The experience was extremely disappointing. Not only was no one there to pick up our luggage on arrival, but the food was also far below expectations. We ordered a pizza that was completely burnt—probably the worst pizza I’ve ever had. On top of that, we were given an incorrect bill calculation twice in the morning. The restaurant was so busy that I couldn’t even get a table for breakfast, and we ended up waiting for a long time. It felt like we were staying in a normal hotel rather than experiencing the five-star service we expected from Taj. We visited with the hope of enjoying top-notch service and food, but that was not what we received., name_person=Riya Jaiswal}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=I went during morning time , they serve good food and drinks.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=However they will have to really work on Coffee and service..}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Great location and perfect for a romantic outing with your partner}"]

The food was excellent specially Khari Toast. In desert we had Dubai’s Kunafa Chocolate Cake, Chocolate Kulfi and Kesar Kulfi. Very yummy.
The decor was tastefully done. The ambiance was family friendly. The service was great thanks to Anees n Pratap.
It’s a pure veg restaurant with Jain menu option. However they serve alcoholic drinks.
Worth visiting., name_person=Balkrishna Shroff}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[9+_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_NINE_OR_MORE], GUIDED_DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS=[No_special_event, E:DINING_SPECIAL_EVENTS_NO_SPECIAL_EVENT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=1}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Service was so so, food was average, but the worst part of this so-called fine dining experience was seeing a mouse roaming inside the restaurant. If this is what you call fine dining, then what’s the difference between this place and a local Irani café? Why charge ₹1,500–₹2,000 per person when basic hygiene is not maintained?

On top of that, it’s extremely noisy — the only good thing here is the ambience, and that alone is not worth risking our health.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Having lived and worked in Japan, albeit many moons ago, I was not expecting to be reminded of the tastes and feel of a typical izakaya in the land of the rising sun, in, of all places, Bandra, Mumbai.
We were ushered to our seating by a raucous welcome from the Kuuraku staff, which was more reminiscent of the Wankhede Stadium than a Japanese restaurant. But there was a effervescence about the staff at Kuuraku, reflecting the confidence that they have in their excellent food.
We ordered the Special Kushi Course, comprising 5 sticks of yakitori. The standout of this was the chicken tail. It was so good that we ordered two extra sticks of this, named bonjiri shio. We also ordered a portion of pork belly yakitori although this was very slightly disappointing as it was a little on the tough side. Another slight disappointment was the chargrilled asparagus wrapped in pork belly. Again, the pork belly wasn't as tender as I expected and the asparagus was a little small and fibrous. However, the edamame challenge was a lot of fun. The idea is to grab as much edamame as possible with one hand - and what you grab is what you get to eat. I used my goalkeeper hands to grab, what the server told me was an over par amount. The edamame was quite good too. The crunchy ebi roll was very generous too coming as a generous portion. The temperature of the rice was spot on as was the consistency. Could the quality of the rice be higher as in Japan? Well yes if you can get that rice but otherwise it really was excellent. The same goes for the pork rice. Here the consistency or the stickiness of the rice was more important than in the ebi roll and if they could get better rice it was be amazing. The slight disappointment was the inclusion of bell peppers. Heresy! Finally, the tea was served in a beautiful black pot, again, very true to Japan.
All in all this was an excellent place with a really true feel of Japan, helped also by the constant stream of Japanese music and the service was particularly excellent. Hopefully they will be more responsible to the society and other customers going forward., name_person=Sonali Shivlani}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=I was looking for a venue for a lazy brunch, and Zomato suggested Bora Bora. I had been there before, quite a while ago, and with a review pending I thought why not, so here goes. I reached to find out that the AC section was closed for renovation, and was given a table outside. The overhead fans were quite efficient, and it wasn't too warm so the lack of AC wasn't an issue for me. I chose the alcoholic menu for their Sunday brunch, and started off with Long Island Iced Tea, Tempura Prawns and Mini Angry Bird. The drink was the first to be served, it was properly chilled, though a little on the sweeter side. Soon the prawns arrived, served fried with mayo and chutney. They weren't too oily, and the chutney went really well with the prawns. Up next was Mini Angry Bird, a veg pizza. Thin crust with tons of cheese, reasonable lot of toppings, a few olives, peppers and capsicum, I enjoyed every bite of it, most recommended, especially for vegetarians. Browsing through the menu the starters seemed really interesting so I decided to stick those and skip the main course. My next order was Chicken Chilly Tacos and Top Secret Malai Kebab, and my next drink was Blenders Pride. The tacos were particularly impressive, spicy meat on toasted bread with cheese, they were an absolute winner. The kebabs weren't too bad either, the meat was tender and though the name said Malai, there was some spice to it, which I didn't mind at all. This was followed by Wild Fish Fingers, strips of basa with a crunchy crust, I found it to be average, have had better elsewhere. With my tummy filling up, I drained my final round of whiskey, and ordered desserts. First up was a platter of pastries, in 3 flavours. The orange pastries were nothing to write about, the red velvet was a little above average, while the kiwi was the by far the best. Next I had some icecream, Vanilla and Strawberry scoops put together and it was delicious, I was tempted to go for another round, but then I was suggested Gulab Jamun by the staff so I opted for that, and what a suggestion it was. The gulab jamuns were soft, sweet and simply superb, a must-have here. Speaking of the staff, I must mention the attendant to my table, Angam. He was most polite, helpful, always with a smile, a big shoutout to his stellar service. With the desserts done, I asked for the cheque to conclude what had been a truly fulfilling meal. To sum up then, Bora Bora offers an excellent brunch, ticks most of the boxes, be it food or drinks or hospitality, there's little to complain. Different members of the kitchen team explained each dish in detail. The team was very passionate and sweet. They also invited us to tour the kitchen and offered my parents a small token for their anniversary. :)

The tasting menu experience easily takes two hours and we are very grateful for the innovative dishes and the hard work behind it.

I am sharing in the pictures a few of the dishes and the menu we ate (the pictures are mostly in order).

In terms of favorities: we really loved the main dishes with the mushroom risotto and sheet pasta with chickpea cutlet. Not to mention the bite size starters were extremely exiting! At no point did we feel the food was too much or not enough. Despite being a 20 course tasting menu it was just right!

We weren't completely in love with the sweets, but maybe that's more on us not having much of a sweet tooth.

Small note: we usually don't have leafs that are already eaten by worms. Despite being heavily processed there is always a chance that their is egg residue left behind. Known for its authentic coastal flavors, this restaurant truly delivers an unforgettable culinary experience with its traditional Gomantak cuisine.

I started with the **Surmai tawa Fry Thali**, and it was a delight. Overall 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻, name_person=Sachin Mumbai}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=We had been looking for a good place to enjoy a Friendship Day lunch, and with a group of 15 friends, Pali Village turned out to be a great choice. The restaurant arranged a sort of private table for us, which made it feel special and comfortable for our large gathering. The ambiance has a nice rustic charm, and it felt like the perfect place to sit back, enjoy conversations, and share a hearty meal.

We began with soups – some of us chose the Cream of Tomato, while a few went for the Vegetable Manchow. The Cream of Tomato was spot on with its rich yet balanced sweetness, smooth consistency, a drizzle of cream, and crunchy breadcrumbs to top it off. It was satisfying and flavorful. However, the Manchow soup was a bit of a letdown – while it had plenty of veggies, it was extra spicy and lacked that signature tang and flavor one usually expects. Adding fried noodles made it slightly better, but overall it fell short compared to the tomato soup.

For starters, we tried a variety – cheese balls, honey chilli potatoes, stuffed mushroom tandoori, and peanut chaat. The cheese balls were the highlight, perhaps the best I’ve had, mainly because they were pure cheese without any fillers like corn. Each bite burst with soft, molten cheese wrapped in a crunchy outer layer – a real treat for cheese lovers. The honey chilli potatoes tasted good but were overwhelmingly spicy despite us asking for medium spice. The stuffed mushrooms were generously portioned and very well received – smoky from the tandoor, with a flavorful paneer and veggie filling. On the other hand, the peanut chaat didn’t quite work for us; it had a vinegar-like coating that felt unusual, making the dish more average than enjoyable.

Moving on to the main course, we ordered Malai Kofta, Paneer Butter Masala, and Veg Handi, along with a mix of rotis, naans, and makai roti. The Malai Kofta was outstanding – rich cashew gravy, creamy but not overly sweet, with soft, perfectly cooked koftas that paired wonderfully with the hot rotis. Both the Paneer Butter Masala and Veg Handi were excellent too. The paneer pieces were soft, with ample portions in the creamy orange gravy, and the dish was made exactly as per our request without coriander. The Veg Handi lived up to its name with a mix of beans, carrots, peas, and cauliflower, all cooked well and full of flavor. The breads were soft, served hot, and generously buttered – the perfect partner to the gravies.

We ended our lunch with a sizzling brownie topped with vanilla ice cream. Though a few desserts we wanted weren’t available, this one made up for it. reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=As the name suggests, a high end premium restaurant located in Atria Mall next to Matahari on level 4, South Bombay Bar was the place I wanted to revisit so eagerly. Had a fabulous experience last time around and it was no different this time around as well. I love the ambiance of the place, well spread, spacious, everyone gets their privacy, yet you always feel right in between action all the time. Just loved how they have painted the ceiling with the map of South Mumbai and well illuminated wall depicting CSTM building structure. A nice mix of high tables, couple tables, comfortable sofa seating, regular tables and chairs section for large groups, just a very well planned layout I must say.

Talking about what all I tried here at South Bombay Bar, I actually just loved everything that was called for -

We started with few appetizers - Mexican Potatoes, Cheese Chilli Garlic Bread and Cheesy Jalapeno Stuffed Mushrooms. I just loved all three of them, but a word of caution for the Mexican Potatoes. Extremely rich in flavours but the Mexican spices also do their wonder. So it's really spicy. We actually asked the chef to tone down the spices, but we still felt it was quite spicy. So those who are in love with spice, this is your treat. I am a big fan of mushrooms and when it's jalapeno and cheese stuffing, it's heavenly. Don't miss this if you eat mushrooms. Last but not the least, we feel you can't go wrong with a chilli cheese toast, but you need to get it right. And that's what you will get here, a safe bet Always.

Along with food, called for couple of drinks - one of my favorites again - Date and Saffron Frappe. I don't think you get this anywhere else and somewhere it's definitely worth travelling and coming here perhaps just for this. Must must try! Also tried the Rosemary Watermelon Iced Tea. Fresh Watermelon is always good to have and a nice blend by the bar tender. Moving on to the mains, we tried the Paneer Londonwala Meal (Tikka Masala gravy) and called for Parathas as our Indian bread option. Just loved this Paneer vegetable one of the best. Meal comes along with papad. Beautiful presentation! After this meal, we had the Dhabewali Dal Khichdi, perfectly made. Light on stomach.

Finally, for desserts - we had Sexin A Tea Pot! Interesting name but I was excited to have this gooey chocolate with vanilla Ice-cream and Orange Zest. That orange flavour right towards the end was super refreshing. Their desserts menu is fabulous - next time around I look forward to having the Blueberry Kulfi and Pinnacotta. Hopefully soon will visit once again. Amazing experience again here!, name_person=Jatin Shah}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=5 years ago, review=This is place has a different but amazing vibe all around. Food 5/5

The Bar is located in one corner, seating is spread in the middle while the DJ plays some peppy tracks on his console from the other end.

Mocktail

Bull frog

Their Food delivers on all fronts in terms of quality, quantity, taste & presentation.

Crisp papadams, tangy pickles, and steaming hot appams completed the meal, while payasam and other Indian sweets brought the feast to a heavenly close.

The carnival bites were the most innovative, and among those, the pani pur semifreddo stood out - it bursts in the mouth where the cold temperature and the flavours work wonders. Bao bhaji is more mundane, with a bhaji stuff bao. So it is a spectrum.

Kala khatta was a salad done on the table, again using liquid nitrogen. Good, but not great. Maybe reduce the kale and the arufula volume?

Kombdi rasa was fabulous with perfectly flavoured rasa. Same is true of the crab krapow, served in a dish shaped as crab. I was looking forward to the much hyped recardo negro, but not sure it lived up to the hype. The flavour of the mutton wasn't as intense as I expected it to be - I am not talking about the chilli heat here. Champaran duck carnitas were good with perfectly cooked duck, but the table side service was pointless. Saffron and parmesan  khichdi had nice flavours but they need to underplay the saffron a bit - it is a very overpowering thing, and subdues all other flavours.

Carnival Celebration dessert was all gimmick. Lot of show but, in the end, a very ordinary chocolate dessert. So much so that we ordered another dessert from the a la carte menu  - aam sutra, with mango foam and mango sorbet, and uniquely textured coconut rasmalai, which was better. Aam Sutra would be even better with something that adds crunch/crispiness for a variety in texture. As far as Carnival Celebration is concerned, I am fine with all tamasha if at the end of it, I get a mind-blowing chocolate dessert.

( We wanted to book at TresInd, but it is closed for renovations so we had to settle for Carnival by Tresind. Also, a restaurant where supplies are being dragged through the hall, Chef Sarfaraz and along with someone just chatting around in casuals, slightly stained aprons of the chefs live dishes - these aren't things that should happen in a high end restaurant. Maybe we missed Tresind!), name_person=Siddhartha Siddhartha}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Carnival by Tresind is a theatrical modern Indian dining jewel in Santacruz west. This place is a visual and sensory delight - dark, luxurious interiors adorned with metallic accents, neon patterns, masks, and rose-gold decor evoke a carnival-like fantasy with a sophisticated edge. Expect mixologists serving up creative cocktails, preparing live at your table. Even some amazing food and tempting dessert are prepared live giving a theatrical flair experience. The mood blends carnival energy with upscale elegance - perfect for special evenings and Sunday lunch with live music.
Drinks are highly inventive, globally inspired, and expertly crafted. Every sip is bold and gives unforgettable experience.
• Global carnival inspiration: Drinks like

2. Chica Picante (Baranquilla carnival inspired) is Spicy and citrusy.
3. Binche G&T  (Binche carnival inspired) is bespoke gin cocktail made live at your table with your choice gin and tonic.
4. Okinawa Sunset (Japanese carnival inspired) is fruity and fizzy.
• More Standout concoctions: Highlights include Java Jamboree (bourbon, espresso, carnival coffee liqueur), Bellino (gin, peach vetiver blanc, bellini ice), MOG (smoky Goan carnival), Scarlet mocktail, and Tiki Tiki with pineapple and hibiscus - visually striking and tastefully bold.
Food and dessert are inventive, bold, flavorful, beautifully plated - modern Indian with a creative twist. Some top picks
• Corn chaat:
• Pani Puri Semifreddo
• Bao Bhaji
• Paneer Tikka Paturi
• Avacado Galouti Kebab
• Nadru Kofta
• Soba Noodles
• Filter Coffee Tiramisu with Baileys Ice Cream: Elegant and rich.
• Aam Sutra: Mango sorbet with coconut ras malai - refreshing and balanced.
Try out its Tasting Menu where “Every dish tells a story”, a carnival of cullinary delights, mind-bending experience throughout from small and big plates to the dessert section.
Service is warm, helpful, and attentive and the staffs are friendly enriching the overall experience. Highly recomended for foodies seeking Fusion surprises and Cocktail lovers looking for conceptual, playful drinks. Overall, Carnival by Tresind is less a meal and more a vibrant performance - where inventive food and cocktail mixology collide.
